Answer: B
Reason: Comparing the initial chest X-ray (Figure 1a), which shows a focal opacity in the right mid-to-lower lung, with the later image (Figure 4), there is clear progression with increased density in the right lung and the appearance of new opacities in the left lung. This pattern of multifocal, progressive consolidation without cavitation or rapid resolution is characteristic of adenocarcinoma in situ (formerly bronchioloalveolar carcinoma), which can present as pneumonia-like infiltrates that spread across lobes or to the contralateral lung.
